key_ok: YouTube key saved: the features that need it can read YouTube.
key_missing: Add your YouTube key in the field below: without it, nothing is read from YouTube.
key_refused: YouTube refuses the key: check it in the field below (the “YouTube Data v3” service must be enabled for it).
key_help: Free key: in the [Google console](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/youtube.googleapis.com), enable “YouTube Data v3”, then create a key under “Credentials” and paste it in the field below.
quota_exhausted: Today's YouTube allowance is used up, back {when}. Meanwhile the site shows the latest data it has.
acc_intro: Connecting your YouTube account is for two things: **answering in the chat** of your live (if you allow it in the advanced options) and **reading the chat** when YouTube refuses to let the site read it with the key alone. You only do it once, and you can disconnect with one click.
acc_none: No YouTube account is connected. It is not needed to read your channel's numbers: follow these 4 steps only to answer in the chat, or if YouTube refuses to let the chat be read with the key.
acc_steps_note: If a name has changed at Google, look for the words in bold: Google's screens change over time.
acc_step1: **Open the Google console** ([console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/)), choose or create a project (the same as for the YouTube key, if you have one) and check that “YouTube Data API v3” is [enabled](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/youtube.googleapis.com) there.
acc_step2: **Prepare the permission screen** in [Google Auth Platform](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview): if Google offers “Get started”, write your site's name and your e-mail address, choose “External”, then finish. Next, in “Audience”, click **Publish app** (without it, the connection stops after 7 days).
acc_step3: **Create the identifier**: in [Clients](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients), click “Create client”, choose the type **TVs and Limited Input devices**, give it a name (your site's name), then “Create”. Google shows the client ID and the client secret: keep that window open.
acc_step4: **Paste them here**: copy the client ID and the client secret into the two fields “Google client ID” and “Google client secret” further down this page, then click “Save”. The “Connect my YouTube account” button then appears at this spot.
acc_bad_id: The client ID does not look like what Google gives: it looks like 123456789-abcdef.apps.googleusercontent.com. Fix it in the field further down.
acc_bad_secret: The client secret looks incomplete (at least 8 characters, no spaces). Paste it again in the field further down.
acc_stale: The client ID has changed since the last connection: connect your account again.
acc_ready: Ready to connect. Google will only ask your permission to read your YouTube chat.
acc_ready_write: Ready to connect. Because “answer in the chat” is on, Google will ask your permission to manage your YouTube account: that is Google's name for the smallest permission that allows writing in a chat. The site only uses it for that.
acc_connected_read: YouTube account connected since {date}. The site can read your live chat with your permission.
acc_connected_write: YouTube account connected since {date}. The site can read your live chat and answer in it.
acc_need_write: You turned on “answer in the chat”, but the permission to write has not been given to Google yet. Connect your account again to give it.
acc_write_idle: The permission to write in the chat is still given to Google, but “answer in the chat” is off in the advanced options: the site writes nothing. To remove the permission, disconnect the account.
acc_disconnect_help: “Disconnect” erases the access kept by the site and tells Google. You can also remove it yourself on [your Google account](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
acc_pending: Code ready: allow the reading of your live chat on your phone.
acc_pending_write: Code ready: on your phone, Google will also ask your permission to write in your chat.
pend_1: On your phone, open {url} (or scan the square next to it).
pend_2: Choose the YouTube account of your channel.
pend_4: Click “Continue”, then “Allow”. If Google says “unverified app”, that is normal: it is your own app. Click “Advanced”, then “Go to…”.
pend_5: Come back here and click “Done, check”. The code is valid for {minutes} more min.
pend_qr_alt: Square to scan to open google.com/device on the phone
connect_started: Code ready. Follow the steps shown.
check_done_write: YouTube account connected, with the permission to write in the chat.
check_pending: Google has not received your permission yet. Finish on your phone, then click again in {seconds} seconds.
disconnect_done: Account disconnected. Google has been told.
disconnect_local: Account disconnected here. Google did not answer: you can also remove the access at myaccount.google.com/permissions.
err_client_id: The client ID is missing or mistyped. Paste it in the “Google client ID” field (it ends with .apps.googleusercontent.com), save, then try again.
err_client_secret: The client secret is missing. Paste it in the “Google client secret” field, save, then try again.
err_too_fast: One moment: wait ten seconds before asking for a new code.
err_too_many: Too many code requests this hour. Try again in an hour.
err_client: Google refuses this client ID or secret. Check them, and that the client type is “TVs and Limited Input devices”.
err_scope: Google did not accept this permission. Check that “YouTube Data API v3” is enabled, then start again and leave the YouTube permission ticked.
err_rate: Google asks for a pause. Try again in a few minutes.
err_timeout: Google is not answering right now. Try again in a few minutes.
err_network: Google is not answering right now. Try again in a few minutes.
err_google: Google answered something unexpected. Start again from the beginning.
err_no_pending: There is no code waiting any more. Click “Connect my YouTube account” to get a new one.
err_expired: The code has expired. Click “Connect my YouTube account” to get a new one.
err_denied: You refused the permission on Google: nothing is connected. Start again if it was a mistake.
err_policy: The chosen account cannot give this permission (a rule of its organisation at Google). Choose your channel's personal account.
last_code_expired: The code expired before it was used. Ask for a new one.
last_denied: You refused the permission on Google: nothing is connected.
last_policy: The chosen account cannot give this permission (a rule of its organisation at Google). Choose your channel's personal account.
last_client: Google refuses the client ID or the secret. Check them in the fields further down, then connect the account again.
last_google: Google answered something unexpected. Start again from the beginning.
last_scope_missing: You unticked the permission on Google's screen: nothing is connected. Start again and leave the box ticked.
last_write_missing: Account connected, but Google did not grant the permission to write in the chat: the site will not be able to answer. Connect the account again and leave the box ticked.
last_expired: Google has removed the account's access (removed from your Google account, or expired). Connect it again.
last_revoke_failed: Account disconnected here, but Google did not answer: you can also remove the access at myaccount.google.com/permissions.
